claims.statement: Shared integration patterns under `docs/integrations/patterns.md` codify that tool-native files are wiring (bootstrap files, rules, MCP config, local preferences) and `.agents/` files are the durable source of truth; product guides keep exact filenames/snippets while shared decisions live once in patterns.md.

Four pattern groups are defined (root AGENTS.md native/compatible; tool-specific bootstrap file; rules-based IDE wiring; persistent memory/runtime boundary) and the session export rule requires exporting durable evidence to `.agents/sessions/<folder>/` at task boundaries for cross-tool distillation instead of relying on private memory.

Agent spread selects exactly one lane per host that should receive integration: `openwiki integrations install <codex|claude|opencode>` for v0.4.3 registry-supported hosts (skill+MCP+receipt atomically), otherwise `npx skills add -g -a <self-reported> langchain-ai/openwiki --full-depth` plus `npx add-mcp -g -a <host>` or `openwiki mcp --host <target>`; default is `~/.agents/skills` (universal, Codex) plus the self-reported host, extra hosts or --all only when the user explicitly asked at install time.

The registry lane `openwiki integrations install <host>` atomically copies the skill bundle to the host skill directory and edits the host MCP config while writing a `.openwiki-install.json` receipt; the MCP is delivered as `openwiki mcp --host <target>` and without this registration the OpenWiki skill is inert.

Receipt `.openwiki-install.json` marks ownership; `openwiki integrations list` reports `installed`/`unchanged` vs `modified` (hand-edits) vs `not-installed` for each host, with user scope by default and `list --project` for repo override.

Before touching any agent skill directory, spread enforces ownership partition via receipt: if `.openwiki-install.json` is present the host is treated as owned by the official lane, skipped entirely, and reported as such; `modified` requires explicit --force to overwrite.

Kit code never hardcodes agent skill paths; all targets are derived at runtime from the registry via `openwiki integrations list` / `inspectInstallation`; bootstrap prefers `openwiki integrations install` where supported and uses `npx skills add -g -a <self-reported>` otherwise to avoid maintaining a path matrix that drifts.

Global ordering is enforced: `openwiki@latest` must be installed and resolvable on PATH before registering `openwiki mcp --host <target>` in host configs; verification is via `openwiki integrations list` returning `installed`/`unchanged` after install.

Bootstrap uses a two-lane execution model (EXECUTE when it can run locally vs INSTRUCT when sandboxed) with never-half-install semantics: a step that cannot execute prints the exact remaining copy-paste commands and exits clean without partial state, and idempotency is by detection of observable state (tools on PATH, `openspec/` present, markers, receipts) not a journal file.

After spread completes a per-agent report is produced naming each detected agent, the lane chosen (`openwiki integrations install <host>` vs headless/unified npx), the outcome (`installed`/`unchanged`/`modified` via `openwiki integrations list`), and installer details including backup path on `--force`.

Canonical user store is `~/.agents/skills` (universal, Codex default) plus the self-reported host's skill directory, installed via `npx skills add -g -a <self-reported> <source>` for the AKSK kit and for `langchain-ai/openwiki --full-depth` when that lifecycle skill is needed; extra agents are installed only if the user explicitly asked for `-a <other>` or `--all` at install time.

`npx` is required for skill installs; the `git clone --depth 1 && cp -r .agents/skills` fallback lane is removed and when `npx` is unavailable bootstrap reports the missing prerequisite via the INSTRUCT lane and does not silently fall back to a copy.

Skill installs use versions from the install version list `references/versions.json` via `versionsFromPackageJson()` (caret range, e.g. `^1.11.0` / `^0.4.3`) when invoking `npx skills add -g -a <self-reported> <source>` for the kit and for `langchain-ai/openwiki`, falling back to `@latest` only when the entry is unpinned.

Verification including `verify-install` treats `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` plus the self-reported host's mirror as the canonical assertion for the default lane; repo-local `./.agents/skills` is an override not the default, and `openwiki integrations list` (user scope) vs `list --project` (repo override) is the scope distinction.

For hosts outside `codex|claude|opencode`, openwiki spread installs the lifecycle skill via `npx skills add -g -a <self-reported> langchain-ai/openwiki --full-depth` and the MCP via `npx add-mcp` (neon-solutions/add-mcp) or `openwiki mcp --host <target>` as the unified fallback.

Global lane (`aksk-bootstrap`) verifies required skills are present in `~/.agents/skills` plus the self-reported host's directory before per-repo work; per-repo scaffolding (`aksk-init`) then runs openspec init, `.agents/` scaffold, and contract/routing attachment. Global lane is global-only and host integrations are manual opt-in.

The kit is packaged as `agent-knowledge-starter` with `package.json` defining `scripts.check` as `bash scripts/check-publish.sh` and pinning `openwiki ^0.4.3` and `@fission-ai/openspec ^1.11.0`; `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` lists the five distributable skills (aksk-bootstrap, aksk-init, task-closeout, learning-distill, docs-lint) and excludes maintainer-only `internal:true` skills such as verify-install.

Install lanes require exactly two supported paths — preferred agent-assisted via `aksk-bootstrap`/`aksk-init` (npx skills add then bootstrap scripts EXECUTE/INSTRUCT) and manual fallback via `npx skills add` — and forbid an `example/` directory or `generate-example` skill/playbook as an install method; bootstrap templates are the source of truth and `scripts/check-publish.sh` validates only root `.agents`.

`scripts/check-publish.sh` is the publish guard: it validates root `.agents` only via `scripts/check-agents-structure.sh .agents`, then runs remark formatting, markdown-link-check per file, rg leakage scans, and doubled `.agents/.agents` hygiene; there is no `example/*` bypass and no `example/.agents` validation target.

Versions for skill-installable packages are pinned in `.agents/skills/aksk-bootstrap/references/versions.json` via `versionsFromPackageJson()` as caret ranges (openwiki ^0.4.3, @fission-ai/openspec ^1.11.0) with consumer `package.json` checked first for override, falling back to `@latest` only when unpinned; `@ferroxlabs/agents-md` is pinned by SHA 90c7198cfa97ff1868f0600952098fee7fc86ef9 in the same file and vendored baseline.

OpenWiki evidence exclusion uses rooted ignores: `.openwikiignore` contains anchored `/example/` (root only, not bare `example/`) and `.agents/sessions/` with `!.agents/sessions/README.md` re-include; root `example/` is a generated consumer-install illustration and `.agents/sessions/` bundles are temporary evidence, neither citable as `repo://` evidence after ignore.
